courses.description: This class will introduce students to various health topics and coursework that will give students the opportunity to become active participants in their own learning process, while meeting each of the health standards. The State of Vermont has switched to learning based proficiency where students can show understanding by demonstrating their knowledge through presentations and role play in groups. Health topics and related skills to be covered include the following: Communication, decision making, goal-setting, accessing valid/scientific information, analyzing influences, health promotion and practice, as well advocacy skills.
courses.notes: Objective: This is a required course and is designed to present current and relevant information about good health habits. It is formatted to help students recognize and make health choices that will enhance the quality and prolong the duration of individual lives.

courses.description: Fashion Design I is an introductory course focused on the apparel and textile industry, specifically exploring design, textiles, and apparel engineering (making clothes). Students will apply design and engineering skills to create and produce apparel products. The course functions from a historical and conservation lens and incorporates art, literacy, math, and science.
courses.notes: Objective: Explore the applied and theoretical concepts needed to construct apparel

courses.description: In this course, students will learn the basics of culinary arts including nutrition, measurement skills, sanitation and safety, food preparation and presentation. Cooking methods and recipe design will be explored through independent project work. This is a hands-on course that requires students to cook and handle food daily, engage in proper food safety and sanitation procedures, and of course, taste many delicious foods from around the world!
courses.notes: Objective: Learn the basics of cooking and food preparation.

courses.description: The folding of a croissant, the lattice work of a pie- your hands will transform butter, sugar, and flour into delicious goods in Baking Arts! Students will learn basic-to-advanced baking techniques, as well as production for a customer-base outside the classroom. Students will learn about dietary restrictions and alternatives to wheat and gluten ingredients. This course is hands-on and students will bake most days! The icing on the cake? All of the taste-testing we will do together.
courses.notes: Objective: Learn the basics of cooking and food preparation.

courses.course_name: Principles of Family and Conservation Sciences: Life Skills
courses.description: Students learn life literacy skills and individual, family, and community systems in support of human flourishing within a community context. Emphasis is placed on human development, professional skills, diversity, analyzing community issues, and life management. Activities engage students in exploring various professions, while building essential life skills they can apply in their own lives to achieve optimal wellbeing. Some of the hands-on learning that will be covered are: how to open a checking account, paying taxes, changing a tire, mending and repairing clothing, and cooking. English/language arts, social studies, mathematics, science, technology, and interpersonal relationships are reinforced. Work-based learning strategies appropriate for this course include service learning and job shadowing.
courses.notes: Objective: Learn life skills that bolster independent living and transitioning from high school to the “real world”.

courses.description: This course provides students with an opportunity to explore the foundational concepts of personal finance. Topics include: career planning, pay, benefits, income taxes, budgeting, record keeping, banking (checking and savings accounts), credit, loans, investing, and insurance.
courses.prerequisites: Pre-Algebra
courses.notes: Objective: To build an understanding of personal finance concepts and how they apply to real-world situations.

courses.description: Each senior explores a topic of personal interest, creates a product to demonstrate their learning, and shares their experience with an audience made up of peers, staff, and community members. The work of Capstone is about research and Portrait of a Learner traits and transferable skills. Students will engage in structured planning, text-based and experiential research, and product design, with a strong focus on communication, problem-solving, and curiosity. This course takes place in the first semester of each academic year.
courses.notes: Objective: Students put into practice the transferable skills they have learned throughout their school years to pursue a topic of their choice. This is a graduation requirement. All seniors finishing their high school in the building will take the capstone course. Those working off campus (CTE, Early College, etc.) will share their learning during presentations in April or May of their graduation year.

courses.description: The program offers students an opportunity to explore different college & career pathways. Through hands-on projects and activities students are introduced to general STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) careers. Students begin their exploration into careers associated with general career pathways, which helps them plan their academic path through grades 11 and 12. The goal of the program is to introduce students to the exciting and often overlooked world of STEM careers, as well as to help them begin to develop their Personal Learning Plans, and walk away with a pathway through graduation and into college and career development. When students are not engaged in a technical activity, they will be in a traditional classroom at RTCC doing ability-appropriate core coursework. Transportation is provided.
courses.prerequisites: Students must apply during 9th grade and be accepted by RTCC
courses.notes: Objective: High school sophomores attend an all-day pre-technical program, offered off campus at RTCC, to “sample” several/all of the technical programs. This experience will help students make a decision on what program to attend during their junior and senior year.; program

courses.description: This is an opportunity for our juniors and seniors to apply their intellect and energy to a specific vocational field of interest. If you are interested in applying to a Career and Technical Education center, see your high school counselor for more details. RTCC programs are full-day and HACTC programs are half-day. Transportation is provided.
courses.prerequisites: To be eligible to apply, students must achieve specific course requirements at WRVHS, attend a CTE presentation, complete an application and be accepted.
courses.notes: Objective: Learn how high school core subject knowledge is applied in the adult working world, through numerous “hands-on” learning opportunities.; program; Length/credit as printed: Full Year (Variable Credits)

courses.description: Community-Based Learning (CBL) provides real-world experiences for students to utilize the community as an extension of the classroom. Through the CBL educator, students aim to secure a work placement or a combination of career exposures. Students set learning goals, document experiences and complete a project. Working with the CBL educator and a community supervisor, students discover future career choices, which may include college plans. To participate, students must be mature and show personal responsibility with limited support. CBL is designed to fit a student’s individual schedule and the availability of a workplace opportunity. This can occur during school, after school, or on weekends or holidays of the school year. Placements typically are one or two in-depth experiences at one or two businesses, but can vary to include a series of exploratory job shadows and career interest interviews. Experiences may be unpaid learning internships, paid entry-level, . Students typically participate for 2 to 6 hours per week, and time may accumulate outside of the school day. Each schedule depends upon agreements between the student, parents/guardians, the mentor/business, and the school.
courses.credits_text: Variable Time (A maximum of 2 CBL credits per year, and 4 CBL credits during high school)
courses.prerequisites: Must demonstrate accountability and self-sufficiency to work off-campus during the school day or after school.
courses.fulfills_text: Allow students to earn elective or academic credit based upon the experiences and projects related to work.
courses.notes: Objective: Allow students to earn elective or academic credit based upon the experiences and projects related to work. This helps students make decisions about future academic and career choices. This course is personalized to fit each student’s schedule and workplace availability.; Grade level as printed: Intended Grade Level: 11-12 (Preferred); program; Length/credit as printed: Variable Time (A maximum of 2 CBL credits per year, and 4 CBL credits during high school)

courses.description: Juniors and seniors may take college courses through participating Vermont institutions, such as CCV, VSU, and Norwich. There is no cost to the student, except for course materials on occasion. These classes count for both high school and college credit, and graduation requirements can be met through taking DE classes (Ex: Taking English 101 at CCV to earn 1 high school English credit to meet graduation requirements).
courses.prerequisites: Desire to take a Dual Enrollment (DE) course must be expressed in the student’s Personalized Learning Plan. College placement testing may be required.
courses.provider: Participating Vermont institutions (e.g., CCV, VSU, Norwich)
courses.fulfills_text: graduation requirements can be met through taking DE classes (Ex: Taking English 101 at CCV to earn 1 high school English credit to meet graduation requirements)
courses.notes: Objective: To expand learning for college and career readiness, juniors and seniors may take two college-level courses.; program

courses.description: This accelerated program for high school seniors offers an exciting alternative and a chance to complete the final year of high school and first year of college at the same time. Participating Vermont institutions include, but are not limited to, CCV, VSU, and Norwich. The classes count for both high school and college credit, and graduation requirements can be met through taking DE classes (Ex: Taking English 101 at CCV to earn 1 high school English credit to meet graduation requirements). Early College is available at specific Vermont Colleges by application and following procedures specific to each school. Tuition is free, leaving the student responsible for associated costs such as applicable fees, book, and supplies (and on-campus residential fees if they choose not to commute). Students must earn a passing “grade” to qualify for high school credit. For more information, see the school counselor.
courses.prerequisites: Completing a college application, possible college placement testing, interview and acceptance.
courses.provider: Participating Vermont institutions (e.g., CCV, VSU, Norwich)
courses.fulfills_text: graduation requirements can be met through taking DE classes (Ex: Taking English 101 at CCV to earn 1 high school English credit to meet graduation requirements)
courses.notes: Objective: To expand learning and college and career readiness through full-time college-level coursework completed during a student’s senior year of high school.; program; Length/credit as printed: Full year (Variable Credits)

courses.description: Because learning happens everywhere, many opportunities for growth and learning exist inside and outside of school. We can build self-contained learning experiences, recognizing and honoring what students do outside the school (on their own or with other organizations), and we can honor academic experiences like the Governor’s Institutes of Vermont. We then weave these experiences together to meet academic proficiencies and other school requirements. Students interested in expanded learning opportunities should be aware that meeting proficiencies sometimes requires work beyond the program, activity, or endeavor.
courses.prerequisites: Permission of the School Counselor and the Flexible Pathways Coordinator. The desire to pursue expanded learning opportunities must be documented in the student’s portfolio.
courses.notes: Objective: As an alternative to traditional coursework, or as enrichment, students might engage in programs outside or inside the school, design and create learning experiences with the guidance of staff members, or pursue their own investigations.; program; Length/credit as printed: Variable Time (Variable Credits)

courses.description: Independent Study options allow students to co-create learning experiences according to their needs and interests, through collaboration with teachers and staff. This starts with student interest, then we explore needs (proficiencies and graduation requirements) and goals (personal, academic, post-high school) to build learning that suits the student. This investigation enables the student to demonstrate proficiencies that would normally be contained within a course. Students interested in independent study should be aware that the work is generally completed independently, with support provided by staff.
courses.prerequisites: Permission of the School Counselor and the Flexible Pathways Coordinator. The desire to pursue independent study must be expressed in the student’s portfolio, and the student will generally plan ahead, consulting with the Flexible Pathways Coordinator during the lead-up to course selection and afterward. Students may access independent study only if the area of study is not offered at WRVHS; or the area of study is offered at WRVHS but cannot fit the student’s schedule.
courses.notes: Objective: As an alternative to traditional coursework, students design and create their own learning experiences with the guidance of staff members.; program; Length/credit as printed: Variable Time (Variable Credits)

courses.description: Students may take courses selected from the Vermont Virtual Learning Cooperative (VTVLC) as part of their high school experience at WRVHS. Work is completed on campus during study halls and at home, following the schedule established by the online teacher. The Flexible Pathways Coordinator can also explore other online options for and with a student. Students may take up to two online courses at the same time.
courses.credits_text: Variable Time (Variable Credits, with a maximum of 2 virtual study credits per year)
courses.prerequisites: Permission of the School Counselor and the Flexible Pathways Coordinator. The desire to pursue virtual study must be expressed in the student’s portfolio, and the student will generally plan ahead, consulting with the Flexible Pathways Coordinator during the lead-up to course selection and afterward. Students may access independent study only if the area of study is not offered at WRVHS; or the area of study is offered at WRVHS but cannot fit the student’s schedule.
courses.notes: Objective: Students choose their own learning experience through an online course not offered in our program of studies.; program; Length/credit as printed: Variable Time (Variable Credits, with a maximum of 2 virtual study credits per year)
